How the game works

The object

Checkmate your opponent's king — put it under attack with no legal way to escape, block, or capture the attacker.

Turns

White moves first, then players alternate. Exactly one legal move per turn; you may never pass.

Check

A king "in check" is under attack. That player must immediately move out of check — no other move is legal.

Checkmate

If a player in check has no legal move to escape it, the game ends immediately — that player loses.

Stalemate

If a player is not in check but has no legal move at all, the game is a draw — nobody wins.

Draws

Games also draw by threefold repetition, the 50-move rule, insufficient material to mate, or mutual agreement.

Castling

A one-time move of king and rook together, for safety and rook activity. Neither piece may have moved, the squares between must be empty, and the king may not pass through check.

En passant

If an opponent's pawn advances two squares and lands beside yours, your pawn may capture it as though it had moved only one square — but only immediately, on the very next move.

Promotion

A pawn reaching the far rank must become a queen, rook, bishop, or knight — almost always a queen, chess's strongest piece.

How each piece moves

Opening principles

Control the center

Squares d4, d5, e4, and e5 give your pieces the most reach. Occupy or influence them early, usually with a central pawn push.

Develop knights before bishops

Knights usually have one clearly best square early on; bishops often want to see how the pawn structure settles first.

Castle early

Get your king to safety and a rook into play in one move, typically within the first six to eight moves.

Don't move a piece twice

Every extra tempo spent replaying a piece is a tempo your opponent gets to develop. Find its good square once.

Keep the queen home, briefly

A queen brought out too early is an easy target for developing minor pieces, costing you time chasing it around.

Connect your rooks

Once the squares between your rooks are clear and your king is castled, your rooks support each other along the back rank.
